subject: Mixed (Real Weightage)
description: 100 questions following the real PGP-CET 2025 subject weightage. Mix: 96 easy / 4 medium / 0 hard. Every question cites its source.

questions.question: The major adverse effect of insulin therapy is:
questions.explanation: Insulin shifts potassium into cells.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: The orthosis usually prescribed for a patient with isolated foot drop is a/an:
questions.explanation: A plastic AFO holds the ankle in neutral and prevents toe drag; KAFO adds the knee, HKAFO the hip.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The hormone responsible for the milk ejection (let-down) reflex is:
questions.explanation: Prolactin stimulates milk production.
questions.sourceBook: D.C. Dutta, Textbook of Obstetrics and Textbook of Gynaecology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Breathlessness specifically occurring when a patient lies flat is termed:
questions.explanation: Orthopnoea is breathlessness specifically triggered by lying flat, classically because it increases venous return from the legs, causing blood to pool in the lungs in cardiac patients. Paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnoea (PND) is a related but distinct pattern — breathlessness that wakes the patient from sleep at night.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which finding is a sign of RIGHT-sided heart failure?

options.B: Raised jugular venous pressure and peripheral oedema

questions.explanation: Left heart failure produces pulmonary congestion (dyspnoea, crackles).
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The nerve most commonly injured in an anterior dislocation of the shoulder is the:
questions.explanation: The axillary nerve winds around the surgical neck of the humerus; test sensation over the ‘regimental badge’ area and deltoid contraction.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A pulse that has two opposite phases (one positive and one negative) within a single pulse is termed:
questions.explanation: Monophasic pulses deviate to one side of the baseline; biphasic pulses have both a positive and negative phase. Symmetrical biphasic pulses have no net polarity.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: On manual muscle testing (MMT), a muscle completes the full available range of motion against gravity alone, but the motion breaks as soon as any additional manual resistance is applied, however mild. What grade should this muscle receive?
questions.explanation: Grade 3 (Fair) is an objective grade: the muscle can complete full range of motion against gravity, but cannot tolerate any added resistance without breaking. Grade 4 requires the muscle to also withstand considerable, though submaximal, resistance.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels and Worthingham's Muscle Testing, 9th ed.
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 1: Principles of Manual Muscle Testing
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Pre-operative physiotherapy for abdominal surgery includes teaching:

options.B: Deep breathing, effective coughing with wound support and leg exercises

questions.explanation: Education before surgery reduces post-operative pulmonary complications and DVT.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Which exercise requires the muscle to work against an external force such as weights, springs or the therapist's hands?
questions.explanation: Resistance increases the load for strengthening: manual, mechanical, isotonic, isometric or isokinetic.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: The earliest morphological change of reversible cell injury is:
questions.explanation: Failure of the Na⁺/K⁺ pump causes influx of water; nuclear changes (pyknosis, karyorrhexis, karyolysis) indicate irreversible necrosis.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: The predominant cell type in acute inflammation is the:
questions.explanation: Macrophages and lymphocytes dominate chronic inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: The Cobb's angle is used to measure:

options.B: The magnitude of scoliosis on X-ray

questions.explanation: Lines are drawn along the upper end-plate of the top vertebra and the lower end-plate of the bottom vertebra of the curve; the angle between perpendiculars is the Cobb angle.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A typically developing infant usually sits without support at about:
questions.explanation: Head control 3–4 months; rolling 4–6; sitting 6–8; crawling 8–10; walking 12–15 months.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The immunoglobulin that crosses the placenta is:
questions.explanation: IgM is the first antibody produced in a primary response; IgA is in secretions.
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology; Ananthanarayan & Paniker, Textbook of Microbiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: According to Ohm's law, the current flowing through a conductor at constant temperature is:

options.A: Directly proportional to the potential difference and inversely proportional to the resistance
options.B: Inversely proportional to the potential difference
options.D: Directly proportional to both the resistance and the potential difference

questions.explanation: Ohm's law: I = V/R. For a given voltage, increasing the resistance reduces the current.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Low-frequency currents used in electrotherapy have frequencies of approximately:
questions.explanation: Low frequency: up to ~1000 Hz. Medium frequency: 1000–10,000 Hz (e.g. interferential, Russian). High frequency: above 10 kHz (shortwave, microwave).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Static stretching involves:

options.A: Slowly lengthening a muscle to the point of mild discomfort and holding the position

questions.explanation: Holding for 15–30 seconds is effective for most adults; it carries less risk of injury than ballistic stretching.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Hepatitis A is transmitted by the:
questions.explanation: Self-limiting; no chronic carrier state.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: The earth wire of a mains cable is conventionally coloured:
questions.explanation: Earth is green/yellow, live is brown (formerly red) and neutral is blue (formerly black). The earth wire connects the metal casing of the apparatus to earth.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The femoral nerve (L2–L4) supplies:
questions.explanation: It passes under the inguinal ligament lateral to the femoral artery.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Genu valgum (knock knee) is a deformity where:

options.A: The knees touch and the ankles are apart
options.C: The knees are apart and the ankles touch

questions.explanation: Physiological genu valgum peaks at 3–4 years; excessive intermalleolar gap needs evaluation.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: ‘Saturday night palsy’ is usually which type of nerve injury?
questions.explanation: Compression of the radial nerve against the humerus (e.g. falling asleep with the arm over a chair) causes a conduction block that recovers spontaneously in weeks.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Immunisation of infants against measles is:
questions.explanation: Vaccination protects before disease occurs.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: How long should postpartum exercises generally be continued for maximal benefit, per standard obstetric guidance?

options.A: Only for the first 24 hours after delivery
options.C: Only once, on the day of discharge
options.D: Postpartum exercise is not recommended at all

questions.explanation: Postpartum exercises — breathing exercises, leg movements, and toning of abdominal, pelvic floor, and back muscles — should be continued for at least 3 months, and are ideally taught by a trained physiotherapist.
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: Hypoglycaemia is generally defined as a blood glucose level below:
questions.explanation: Symptoms: sweating, tremor, confusion; treat with oral glucose or IV dextrose.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: SWD should NOT be applied to a patient with:

options.C: A cardiac pacemaker or metal implants in the field

questions.explanation: Metal implants and pacemakers concentrate or are disturbed by the field; other contraindications include pregnancy, malignancy, impaired circulation or sensation, haemorrhage, and moisture over the field.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The most reliable method of sterilising surgical instruments is:
questions.explanation: Autoclaving at 121 °C for 15 minutes (or 134 °C for 3 minutes) kills spores.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: Strokes are broadly classified into two main categories based on underlying pathology:
questions.explanation: Strokes are broadly classified as ischemic (from thrombus, embolism, or low systemic perfusion depriving brain tissue of blood flow) or hemorrhagic (from rupture of a cerebral vessel causing bleeding into or around the brain).
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan, Physical Rehabilitation
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The ‘Russian current’ used for strengthening muscle is characterised by:

options.C: A direct current delivered in 100 ms pulses
options.D: A 2500 Hz medium-frequency carrier delivered in 50 bursts per second

questions.explanation: Kots’ Russian stimulation is a 2500 Hz sine carrier interrupted into 10 ms bursts (50 per second, 50% duty cycle), used to strengthen normal muscle.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Ober's test is performed to identify tightness of the:

options.B: Iliotibial band and tensor fasciae latae

questions.explanation: Side-lying; hip abducted and extended then lowered; failure of the thigh to drop below horizontal indicates ITB/TFL tightness.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The hallmark of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease on spirometry is:

options.A: A reduced FEV1/FVC ratio (below 70%) that is not fully reversible

questions.explanation: COPD: persistent airflow limitation; FEV1/FVC <0.70 post-bronchodilator.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Gowers' sign, in which a child uses the hands to ‘walk up’ the thighs to stand, indicates weakness of the:

options.B: Pelvic girdle and proximal lower limb muscles

questions.explanation: Typical of Duchenne muscular dystrophy (X-linked dystrophin deficiency); calf pseudohypertrophy is also seen.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A wheelchair user with SCI should perform a pressure-relief lift about every:
questions.explanation: Regular pressure relief and repositioning prevents ischaemia over the ischial tuberosities; 2-hourly turns are used in bed.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: De Quervain's tenosynovitis involves the tendons of:

options.A: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
options.B: Flexor pollicis longus and flexor carpi radialis
options.C: Extensor carpi ulnaris and extensor digiti minimi
options.D: Extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis

questions.explanation: The first dorsal compartment is inflamed; Finkelstein's test (ulnar deviation with thumb flexed in palm) reproduces pain over the radial styloid.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The most commonly used frequency for therapeutic shortwave diathermy (SWD) is:
questions.explanation: SWD uses 27.12 MHz (11 m); 13.56 MHz and 40.68 MHz are also allocated. 2450 MHz belongs to microwave diathermy.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Vitamin B6 collectively refers to which three related pyridine-derivative compounds?
questions.explanation: Vitamin B6 collectively represents three related pyridine-derivative compounds — pyridoxine (a primary alcohol form), pyridoxal (an aldehyde form), and pyridoxamine (an amine form) — which can interconvert, and are together known as the vitamers of B6.
questions.sourceBook: Satyanarayana, Biochemistry
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Free (active) exercises are movements:

options.B: Performed by the patient's own muscles without external resistance, assistance or apparatus loading

questions.explanation: Free exercises are classified as local or general and include mobilising, strengthening and coordination exercises.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: A hydrocele is:

options.A: A collection of fluid within the tunica vaginalis
options.C: A varicosity of the pampiniform plexus

questions.explanation: Hydroceles are translucent and one can get above the swelling.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: The reaction produced beneath the cathode when direct current is passed through the tissues is:
questions.explanation: Under the cathode (−) sodium hydroxide forms → alkaline reaction, which is more irritant and liquefies tissue. Under the anode (+) hydrochloric acid forms → acidic reaction, which hardens tissue.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: McBurney's point lies:

options.A: At the midpoint of the inguinal ligament
options.B: Midway between the umbilicus and symphysis pubis
options.D: One-third of the distance from the right ASIS to the umbilicus

questions.explanation: Maximal tenderness here suggests appendicitis.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: A motor unit consists of:

options.A: A sensory neurone and a muscle
options.B: A motor neurone and all the muscle fibres it innervates

questions.explanation: Muscles of fine control (e.g. eye muscles) have small motor units.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Most levers in the human body are:

options.C: Third-class, in which the effort lies between the axis and the resistance

questions.explanation: Example: biceps brachii flexing the elbow. They favour speed and range of motion over force.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Hacking, clapping, cupping and beating are movements of:
questions.explanation: Percussion stimulates tissue and is used in chest physiotherapy to loosen secretions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Phalen's test (wrist flexion held for 60 seconds) is positive in:
questions.explanation: Sustained wrist flexion compresses the median nerve, producing paraesthesia in its distribution in carpal tunnel syndrome.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Penicillins act by:

options.A: Inhibiting protein synthesis at the 30S subunit

questions.explanation: Anaphylaxis is the most serious adverse effect.
questions.sourceBook: K.D. Tripathi, Essentials of Medical Pharmacology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Pharmacology

questions.question: A Grade V Maitland movement is:

options.B: A passive stretch within pain-free range
options.C: A small-amplitude, high-velocity thrust at the end of range

questions.explanation: Manipulation: small-amplitude, high-speed thrust beyond the elastic barrier, often with an audible cavitation.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The typical upper limb posture in spastic hemiplegia is:

options.A: Shoulder lateral rotation and wrist extension
options.B: Shoulder abduction, elbow extension and forearm supination
options.D: Shoulder adduction/internal rotation, elbow flexion, forearm pronation and wrist/finger flexion

questions.explanation: Flexor synergy dominates the arm; extensor synergy dominates the leg (hip extension/adduction, knee extension, plantar flexion with inversion).
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: A 'repetition maximum' (RM), as first described by DeLorme, is defined as:

options.A: The greatest amount of weight a muscle can move through full available ROM a specific number of times before fatiguing
options.B: The maximum number of exercise sessions a patient can complete in a week
options.C: The total duration in months of a resistance training program
options.D: A measure of joint range of motion only

questions.explanation: A repetition maximum (RM) is the greatest amount of weight (load) a muscle can move through the full available range of motion, with control, a specific number of times before fatiguing — e.g. a '10-RM' is the maximum weight that can be lifted through 10 repetitions.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The frequency of microwave diathermy used therapeutically is:
questions.explanation: Microwaves occupy 300 MHz–30 GHz; therapeutic units use 2450 MHz (12.25 cm), 915 MHz or 433.9 MHz.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The earliest symptom of vitamin A deficiency is:
questions.explanation: Progression: night blindness, conjunctival xerosis, Bitot's spots, corneal xerosis, keratomalacia.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Ergonomics is the study of:

options.C: The relationship between workers and their working environment to improve efficiency and reduce injury

questions.explanation: Applies to workstation design, posture, lifting and repetitive tasks.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: The standard position to test grade 3 knee extension (quadriceps) is:

options.A: Sitting with the knee over the edge of the plinth, extending the knee against gravity

questions.explanation: Sitting (thigh supported) lets the patient extend the knee against gravity; resistance is given at the distal leg for grade 4–5.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: A 15-year-old active boy has pain and a prominent tibial tubercle for 4 months with no systemic illness. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.explanation: Traction apophysitis of the tibial tubercle from repeated quadriceps pull; self-limiting, treated with activity modification and stretching.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A steppage (high-stepping) gait is seen in:
questions.explanation: Foot drop needs excessive hip and knee flexion to clear the toes; seen in common peroneal palsy, L4–L5 radiculopathy.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: The carrying angle at the elbow is decreased (arm adducted more) in:
questions.explanation: Cubitus varus (‘gunstock deformity’) results from malunion of a supracondylar fracture, reducing the carrying angle.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: Stride length is the distance between:

options.B: Two successive heel strikes of the same foot
options.C: Heel strike of one foot and the other foot

questions.explanation: Stride = two steps; step length = distance between consecutive heel strikes of opposite feet.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Incidence of a disease refers to:

options.A: The number of NEW cases occurring in a population during a specified period
options.B: All existing cases at a point in time

questions.explanation: Prevalence = all existing cases (old + new); prevalence ≈ incidence × mean duration.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine; WHO/ICF and CBR guidelines; standard biostatistics/research methodology texts (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 6 Research and Analysis)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: Intermittent claudication is calf pain that:

options.C: Occurs on walking a fixed distance and is relieved by rest

questions.explanation: Caused by atherosclerotic arterial insufficiency; supervised walking programmes improve walking distance.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Ankylosing spondylitis is strongly associated with:
questions.explanation: HLA-B27 is positive in ~90% of patients. It starts in the sacroiliac joints and ascends, giving the ‘bamboo spine’ on X-ray.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: According to the New York Heart Association (NYHA) classification of breathlessness, a patient who becomes symptomatic with mild exertion such as bathing or dressing falls into which class?
questions.explanation: NYHA Class III describes symptoms occurring with mild exertion (e.g. bathing, showering, dressing). Class I is asymptomatic except with severe exertion, Class II is symptomatic with ordinary activity (e.g. walking upstairs), and Class IV is symptomatic even at rest.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: Guillain–Barré syndrome typically presents with:

options.A: Ascending symmetrical flaccid weakness with areflexia after an infection

questions.explanation: An acute inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy; CSF shows raised protein with normal cell count (albuminocytological dissociation).
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: Medium-frequency currents have a frequency of:
questions.explanation: Interferential and Russian currents are medium-frequency currents (typically carrier 2000–4000 Hz).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: Consolidation of the lung is associated with:

options.B: Stony dullness with decreased vocal resonance
options.C: Bronchial breathing, dull percussion note and increased vocal resonance

questions.explanation: Solid lung conducts sound better: bronchial breath sounds, whispering pectoriloquy, dull note.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The most important complication to watch for after applying a tight plaster cast is:
questions.explanation: Warn patients about increasing pain, swelling, numbness; elevate the limb.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics

questions.question: A normal resting adult respiratory rate is approximately:
questions.explanation: Normal adult resting HR 60–100 bpm, RR 12–20/min, BP <120/80 mmHg, SpO₂ 95–100%.
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: In adult cardiac arrest the correct compression-to-ventilation ratio for CPR is:
questions.explanation: Compress at 100–120 per minute to a depth of 5–6 cm.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: A knee moves from 15° of flexion (cannot extend further) to 90° of flexion. The total available range of motion is:
questions.explanation: Total arc = end − start = 90 − 15 = 75°. It would be recorded as 15–90° (extension lag/flexion contracture of 15°).
questions.sourceBook: Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physical Diagnosis & Manipulative Skills

questions.question: Post-operative atelectasis is MOST effectively prevented by:

options.B: Early mobilisation, deep breathing exercises and incentive spirometry

questions.explanation: Reduced lung volumes after anaesthesia and pain contribute; early ambulation and deep breathing restore functional residual capacity.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The commonest cause of duodenal ulcer is:
questions.explanation: NSAIDs are the second most important cause; treat with triple therapy.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Which two special tests are classically used to assess for a meniscal injury of the knee?

options.B: Lachman test and pivot shift test
options.C: Clarke's sign and the Q-angle measurement
options.D: Noble compression test and Ober's test

questions.explanation: The McMurray test and Apley's (compression/distraction) test are the classic special tests for meniscal injury of the knee, alongside the 'bounce home' test.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment
questions.sourceChapter: Chapter 12: Knee — Special Tests Commonly Performed on the Knee
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The correct handgrip height of an axillary crutch is such that the elbow is flexed about:
questions.explanation: Check at the greater trochanter or the wrist crease; the axillary pad is 4–5 cm below the axilla to prevent crutch palsy.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise: Foundations and Techniques; Dena Gardiner, Principles of Exercise Therapy; Tidy's Physiotherapy (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Exercise Therapy

questions.question: Which of the following is a vector quantity?
questions.explanation: Vectors have magnitude and direction (force, velocity, acceleration, displacement); scalars have magnitude only (mass, speed, distance, time).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The corpus callosum's main function is to:

options.A: Produce hormones for the endocrine system
options.B: Connect corresponding areas of the cortex in one cerebral hemisphere with the other hemisphere
options.C: Carry sound information from the ear to the temporal lobe

questions.explanation: The corpus callosum is a large bundle of nerve fibers that connects corresponding areas of the cortex in the left and right cerebral hemispheres, allowing communication and integration between the two sides of the brain.
questions.sourceBook: Morgan & King, Introduction to Psychology
questions.sourceChapter: Biology of Behavior — Forebrain: Cerebrum, Structure
questions.subject: Psychology

questions.question: Mean arterial pressure is approximately:

options.C: Diastolic pressure plus one-third of the pulse pressure

questions.explanation: MAP = DBP + (SBP−DBP)/3; e.g. 120/80 → 93 mmHg.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: According to the framework for 'asking questions' in epidemiology, which of the following is a question 'related to health action' rather than 'related to health events'?

options.B: What resources are required, and how are activities to be organized?

questions.explanation: Questions like 'what is the event', 'where/when did it happen', and 'who is affected' are related to health events. Questions about what resources are required and how activities should be organized fall under questions related to health action — what should be done about the problem.
questions.sourceBook: Park's Textbook of Preventive and Social Medicine
questions.sourceChapter: Principles of Epidemiology and Epidemiologic Methods — Asking Questions
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Community Health

questions.question: An antalgic gait is characterised by:

options.B: A prolonged stance on the painful limb
options.D: A shortened stance phase on the painful limb

questions.explanation: The patient reduces weight-bearing time on the painful limb.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: The average lifespan of a red blood cell is:
questions.explanation: Old RBCs are removed by the spleen.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: Agoraphobia, the commonest type of phobia seen in clinical practice, is best described as:

options.A: Fear limited strictly to open spaces only
options.B: Irrational fear of being in places away from the familiar setting of home, including crowded or public places with no easy escape
options.D: Fear of being watched while performing in public

questions.explanation: Agoraphobia was once thought to be simply a fear of open spaces, but it is now understood more broadly as an irrational fear of being away from the familiar safety of home — including open spaces, public places, crowded places, or anywhere escape to safety feels difficult.
questions.sourceBook: Ahuja, A Short Textbook of Psychiatry
questions.sourceChapter: Neurotic, Stress-related and Somatoform Disorders — Phobic Disorder
questions.subject: Psychiatry

questions.question: The topical agent commonly used on burn wounds to prevent infection is:
questions.explanation: Silver sulfadiazine has broad antibacterial activity including Pseudomonas; mafenide is an alternative.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: On the Glasgow Coma Scale, what is the maximum total score, and what does it represent?

options.B: 15, representing a fully alert, orientated patient

questions.explanation: The Glasgow Coma Scale has a maximum total score of 15 (best possible — eye opening 4, verbal response 5, motor response 6), representing full alertness, and a minimum score of 3, representing the deepest level of unresponsiveness.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The nerve that supplies the lateral rectus muscle of the eye is the:
questions.explanation: LR6 SO4 and the rest are supplied by the oculomotor nerve.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Diabetes mellitus is diagnosed when the fasting plasma glucose is:
questions.explanation: Also HbA1c ≥ 6.5%, random glucose ≥ 200 mg/dL with symptoms, or 2-h OGTT ≥ 200 mg/dL.
questions.sourceBook: Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference); standard internal medicine texts
questions.subject: Medicine

questions.question: Vitamin K is required for:

options.C: Gamma-carboxylation of clotting factors II, VII, IX and X

questions.explanation: Warfarin inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase.
questions.sourceBook: U. Satyanarayana, Biochemistry; Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Biochemistry

questions.question: Multiple sclerosis is a disease of:
questions.explanation: MS: autoimmune demyelination in the CNS with episodes disseminated in time and space.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The wavelength range of UVB is:
questions.explanation: UVA 315–400 nm; UVB 280–315 nm; UVC 100–280 nm. UVB is the main erythemogenic and vitamin D–forming band.
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The Moro reflex normally disappears by about:
questions.explanation: Persistence of the Moro reflex beyond 6 months suggests neurological abnormality. ATNR disappears by ~6 months, palmar grasp by 4–6 months.
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The primary hip abductors are the:

options.C: Gluteus medius, gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae

questions.explanation: Innervated by the superior gluteal nerve (L4–S1).
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: Carpal tunnel syndrome is caused by compression of the:

options.A: Radial nerve at the spiral groove

questions.explanation: Compression beneath the flexor retinaculum produces night pain and tingling in the thumb, index, middle and radial half of the ring finger; thenar wasting is late.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: The active cycle of breathing technique (ACBT) consists of:

options.D: Breathing control, thoracic expansion exercises and the forced expiration technique

questions.explanation: ACBT cycles include breathing control (relaxed tidal breathing), deep breathing exercises and huffing (FET), repeated until the chest is clear.
questions.sourceBook: Pryor & Prasad, Physiotherapy for Respiratory and Cardiac Problems; ACSM Guidelines; Davidson's Principles and Practice of Medicine (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in General Medical & Surgical Condition

questions.question: The hamstring muscles arise from the:
questions.explanation: Except the short head of biceps femoris, which arises from the linea aspera.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: Which strategy helps overcome freezing of gait in Parkinson's disease?

options.B: External cues such as floor lines or a rhythmic beat

questions.explanation: Visual and auditory cues exploit intact cortical-cerebellar pathways to bypass the basal ganglia deficit (kinesia paradoxa).
questions.sourceBook: O'Sullivan & Schmitz, Physical Rehabilitation; standard neurology/neurorehabilitation texts (chapter-level reference; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Neurosciences

questions.question: The atlantoaxial (median) joint is a:
questions.explanation: Rotation of the atlas about the dens of the axis gives 50% of cervical rotation.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Neumann, Kinesiology of the Musculoskeletal System; Daniels & Worthingham (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 3 Biomechanics)
questions.subject: Kinesio Therapeutics

questions.question: After a posterolateral approach total hip replacement the patient should be advised to AVOID:

options.A: Hip flexion beyond 90°, adduction past the midline and internal rotation
options.D: Sleeping with a pillow between the knees

questions.explanation: Posterior approach precautions prevent dislocation: no flexion >90°, no crossing legs, no internal rotation. Use raised chairs/toilet seats and a pillow between the legs.
questions.sourceBook: Kisner & Colby, Therapeutic Exercise; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics; Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment (facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)
questions.subject: Physiotherapy in Musculoskeletal Condition

questions.question: A device used to regulate (vary) the current in a circuit by altering its resistance is called a:
questions.explanation: A rheostat is a variable resistor. Changing its resistance changes the current flowing in the circuit (Ohm's law, I = V/R).
questions.sourceBook: Clayton's Electrotherapy; facts cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination (2nd ed.), Ch. 2 Electrotherapy
questions.subject: Fundamentals of Electro Therapy

questions.question: The brachial plexus is formed by the ventral rami of:
questions.explanation: Roots C5–T1 → trunks (upper, middle, lower) → divisions → cords (lateral, medial, posterior) → branches.
questions.sourceBook: B.D. Chaurasia's Human Anatomy (Upper Limb, Lower Limb, Thorax, Head & Neck, Neuroanatomy) — chapter-level reference
questions.subject: Anatomy

questions.question: The reddish vaginal discharge seen in the first 1-4 days after delivery is called:
questions.explanation: Lochia progresses through three stages by colour: lochia rubra (red, days 1-4), lochia serosa (yellowish/pink/pale brownish, days 5-9), and lochia alba (pale white, days 10-15).
questions.sourceBook: Dutta's Textbook of Obstetrics
questions.subject: OBGY

questions.question: The two basic components present in every tumour (benign or malignant) are the parenchyma and the:
questions.explanation: Every tumour has parenchyma (the proliferating tumour cells themselves, which determine the tumour's nature and behaviour) and a supportive stroma (fibrous connective tissue and blood vessels that provide the structural framework for the parenchymal cells to grow on).
questions.sourceBook: Harsh Mohan, Textbook of Pathology
questions.subject: Pathology & Microbiology

questions.question: In a normal ECG the QRS complex represents:
questions.explanation: P wave: atrial depolarisation; T wave: ventricular repolarisation.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
questions.subject: Physiology

questions.question: The most common organism causing acute haematogenous osteomyelitis in children is:
questions.explanation: Metaphysis of long bones (rich vascularity, sluggish flow) is the typical site; Salmonella is seen in sickle cell disease.
questions.sourceBook: Bailey & Love's Short Practice of Surgery; Maheshwari, Essential Orthopaedics (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e, Ch. 4 Orthopedics)
questions.subject: General Surgery & Orthopedics
